text:
alex: FYI — ran a small experiment on microburst probing + deferred backpressure this morning. results look promising but there are tradeoffs.

maria: quick summary?

alex: goal was to avoid immediate backpressure on tiny microbursts (10-50 reqs) so we let a light probing window open for ~8-12ms and only apply hard backpressure if sustained.

simon: so you basically debounce the backpressure? how do you prevent one tenant from gaming the probe?

alex: two levers: 1) probe budget per-tenant (tokens) that slowly refills, 2) exponential probe penalty if probes hit queued-eviction repeatedly. keeps gaming costy.

lee: curious about fairness impact — do we add long-tail latency for others while probe runs?

alex: short answer: sometimes. small increase in p99 when probes are open, but p50/p95 improved for many small-req workloads because they avoid full admission failures.

tara: interesting. can you paste the config you used?

alex: here:

```
batching.microburst_probing.enabled = true
batching.microburst_probing.window_ms = 10
batching.microburst_probing.max_probe_tokens = 3
batching.deferred_backpressure.enabled = true
batching.deferred_backpressure.grace_ms = 12
probe.penalty.base_ms = 20
probe.penalty.multiplier = 2.0
```

maria: thanks. what telemetry did you look at to decide 10-12ms?

alex: CPU/queue-depth histograms + end-to-end latency buckets per tenant. we also profiled kernel enqueue/dequeue jitter and saw a knee around 8-15ms for burst consolidation on our GPU pools.

simon: any safety nets? if probe causes starvation we should have an escape hatch.

alex: yes — two escape paths: 1) global hard cap on probe concurrency (configurable), 2) an emergency short-circuit that flips to immediate backpressure when p99 for any tenant climbs > SLO threshold in a 30s window. ops-bot logs that flip.

ops-bot: deploybot: experiment branch "microburst-probe-v2" rolled to staging at 2026-03-23T09:12:00Z. monitor /eng-runtime/telemetry/microbursts.

lee: how does this interact with KV cache warmups? early probes might cause wasted KV state warmups.

alex: good call — we tag probe requests so runtime treats them as warmup-ineligible (no KV allocation) unless probe succeeds and transitions to normal admission. reduces warmup churn.

tara: what about batching efficiency? more small probes could reduce packing density.

alex: yes, but net effect depends on request size distribution. for strongly microbursty traffic (lots of 1-5 token reqs) probing increases throughput by avoiding full queue thrash. for steady heavy streams it slightly reduces packing, so we gate per-tenant by historical packing score.

maria: action items?

alex: 1) more A/B to tune grace_ms and probe tokens (owner: alex)
 2) add a telemetry panel: probe_open_ratio, probe_penalty_count, p50/p95/p99 delta (owner: simon)
 3) add feature flag + emergency short-circuit hook (owner: lee)
 4) docs + QA for KV-tagging semantics (owner: tara)

simon: +1 on telemetry. include tenant-level heatmap so we can spot gaming.

tara: I'll draft the KV-tagging doc and a short checklist for QA.

lee: create a follow-up thread when we have A/B numbers. also let's snapshot trace samples for probe vs non-probe paths.

alex: will do. logging note: keep probe traces low-sample (1%) to avoid noise.

maria: thanks everyone. sounds like a reasonable path forward — cautious rollout, telemetry first. :thumbsup:

alex: cheers. I'll push a new branch with metric names and the feature flag by EOD.
